done_when: A fix that changes a forge.toml setting other than merge keeps that change through close and review, or close refuses with a clear reason instead of reporting ready.

known.title: Not done: A settings fix can reach Ready after its change is lost
Give a usable next step when main already contains the fix
Follow-up: Tasks can reach Ready after their changes are removed

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - Forge carries a waiting idea into a settings fix, and a later merge replaces the fix's test setting.
The Done-when item is: “A fix that changes a forge.toml setting other than merge keeps that change through close and review, or close refuses with a clear reason instead of reporting ready.” Forge can carry `plans/ideas.md` into a new fix (`src/forge/intake.py:153-164`). If that is the only surviving change besides the fix record, `require_fix_changes` counts it as product work and returns at `src/forge/task.py:745-747`, before the new refusal. Close then classifies it as bookkeeping, skips review and can report Ready (`src/forge/close.py:299-301,354-361`). Client-signoff decision files have the same mismatch. The requested setting can therefore be lost while close reports no product change to review.
findings.title: Not done: A settings fix can reach Ready after its change is lost

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - the default branch upgrades Forge while a settings fix is underway.
The named preservation proof changes only the comment beside the version, leaving the actual pin unchanged. Its changes merge cleanly, and with the fixture's absent pull request, `src/forge/close.py:754-756` leaves main unmerged. The test also does not inspect the change sent to review. It can pass while merging a real pin change loses the setting, so it does not prove the requested merge-and-review behavior.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_close_keeps_fix_settings.py::test_1_close_keeps_the_fix_test_setting_after_main_moves_the_pin

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - another change lands the same fix on the default branch before close.
The new refusal says main may already have the change but nevertheless tells the user to make it again and commit. In that case repeating the edit produces no product diff, so the suggested action cannot clear the refusal. `tests/test_close_reviews_only_product_changes.py:15-27` sets up this exact situation. The refusal needs guidance that also handles work already delivered on main.
Adds work: provide an actionable next step for already-delivered fixes; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2.
findings.title: Give a usable next step when main already contains the fix

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - a task's implementation disappears while its branch is reconciled with the default branch.
The new history check applies only to fixes: `src/forge/task.py:743-744` returns immediately for tasks. With only task records left, `src/forge/close.py:299-301,354-361` skips review and can mark the task Ready despite the lost implementation.
Adds work: detect a task whose implementation disappeared before reporting it ready; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4.
findings.title: Follow-up: Tasks can reach Ready after their changes are removed

why: A fix that changes a forge.toml test setting (other than merge) loses that change before close, and close still reports the pull request ready with no real change.
